loss_details: Enemy fighters knocked out engines #3 and #4 (91-01; the MACR text quoted there also says No. 4 feathered and No. 1 smoking). Seen at 1530 hrs from 20,000 ft at 48°40'N 06°40'E descending under control, four parachutes seen (observer 2nd Lt. Joseph A. Sulli). Crash-landed on a rail line south of Metz, France; salvaged by the Luftwaffe and used by KG 200 for spares.
notes: Nickname given as 'Old Faithful II' (91-01 title) and 'Old Faithful' (91-02, IWM). Ex-306th BG 423rd BS (RD-S), to 91st BG 323rd BS 11 Sep 1943; 91-01/91-02 also list 322nd BS code LL-S (conflicting / other period). Squadron code+letter OR-N is from 91-01, not confirmed for this date. Crew names in 91-01 are informal (Bob, Joe, Art...). MACR 899 itself not consulted.

loss_details: Battle damaged over Schweinfurt; pilot Lt Christensen wounded and died the next day. Co-pilot Lt Mendelsohn flew it back and crash-landed at RAF Tangmere, striking a tree. Not struck off: after a long repair it returned to service with the 401st BS (LL-D) (91-01, 91-02).
notes: Crash-landed in the UK, long repair (not written off). Letters given only as 'DF-F/D/P' (91-01), so the aircraft letter on this date is unknown. Whether it bombed the target is not documented (the IWM Christensen narrative describes an abort - conflict).

loss_details: Brought down by enemy aircraft; crashed at St Goar, 11 miles SE of Boppard, Germany. All 10 crew POW.
notes: Two independent databases (92-01, 92-02) agree on serial, MACR 844, crash site and crew. 92-01 lists the first unit as '325th BS, 95th BG, NV-Z' - the 325th BS and code NV are 92nd BG, and 92-02 says 325th BS/92nd BG, so the '95th BG' tag in 92-01 is treated as an error. Code JW-O after transfer to 326th BS (date of transfer not given; squadron on 14 Oct 1943 per IWM person record of Bomberger = 326th).

loss_details: Missing in action; downed by enemy aircraft and crashed near Würzburg, Germany. 3 KIA (bodies never recovered), 7 POW.

loss_details: Attacked by enemy fighters after leaving the target (92-01 says 'Fw110'); last seen at 13:40 (location given as near Düren), exploded and crashed near Kembach, about 15 miles W of Würzburg. Credited to Fw. Joachim Gutmann, 8./ZG 26. 6 KIA, 4 POW.
notes: Code PY-X (92-02); 92-01 gives PY-X/S. Last-seen location 'near Düren' is geographically odd for a crash near Würzburg - recorded as given.

loss_details: Missing in action, attributed to enemy aircraft; crashed at Sickershausen, SE of Kitzingen, about 12 miles SE of Würzburg. 5 KIA, 5 POW. Tail gunner Nelson W. Smith reportedly did not bail out and was killed in the radio room (92-04).

loss_details: Not lost. 92-06 says McLaughlin's lead bomber returned with an engine on fire after pursuit by fighters.

Budd Peaslee's B-17 'Equipose/Equipoise', flown by lead pilot Kemp McLaughlin, led the 92nd. 42-30580 'Equipoise' (326th BS, JW-N) exists in the IWM archive (photographed with 'Lt McLaughlin and crew' 25 Sep 1943) but its record does not mention 14 Oct 1943. McLaughlin as lead pilot on the raid is documented in 92-06 (rank Captain). Col. Budd Peaslee flew aboard as air commander per 92-05.

loss_details: Enemy aircraft knocked out one engine, a second attack damaged another; bombs jettisoned; tracers knocked out a third engine; ditched in the North Sea about five miles from the UK; crew rescued within an hour (10 RTD). Matches AAM mission summary '10RTD (rescued by ASR)'.
notes: Aircraft lost (ditched) but crew rescued. Did not bomb (bombs jettisoned). No MACR found. Crew list in source incomplete: engineer, ball, one waist and tail gunner unknown. AAM also links S/Sgt Severin Henry Rodeschin (waist gunner, 332nd BS) and S/Sgt Orville J Draeger to this airframe, but not to this date - UNVERIFIED, not added to crew. loss_details: Shot down by enemy aircraft while heading for Switzerland; crashed in Lake Barmsee near Mittenwald, Germany. 9 POW, co-pilot KIA.
notes: Squadron/code CONFLICT: history says 'Assigned 339BS/96BG [IJ- ] ... transferred 337BS [QJ- ]' (QJ was the 339th code); all AAM crew person records list 339th BS. Squadron recorded as 339th; code and letter left null. b17flyingfortress.de block field lists both B-17F-75-DL and B-17G-5-DL for the range; F-75-DL recorded as the aircraft is a B-17F.

loss_details: Battle damage; pilot killed by a shell in the cockpit, co-pilot wounded; flown back by the navigator and bombardier and landed at RAF Ford, Sussex; salvaged 20/10/43. (Source also says 'Returned to the USA 121 BU Bradley 31/7/44' - contradictory.)
